Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/21/2026
Patient: Lean Stanton, 65 y/o F

Attended PSG 04/21/2026. Study revealed severe sleep-disordered breathing. Total AHI 50.6/h. CA+MA 4% of total AHI. Oxygen desaturation nadir 82%. Sleep architecture fragmented with reduced REM and slow wave sleep. Periodic limb movements within normal limits. No significant arrhythmias noted. CPAP titration recommended based on findings.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/12/2026
Patient: Lean Stanton, 65 y/o F

Hx: OSA dx 2018, CPAP started 2019. Pt reports poor adherence.

CPAP dl avg 2.4 h/night, 45% nights despite mask refit; SDM w/ pt: CPAP intolerant.

Exam: BMI 32, no craniofacial abnormalities. No nasal obstruction noted.

Plan: Discussed alternatives to CPAP including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy. Sleep hygiene reinforced. Referral to dental sleep specialist made.

F/U in 3 mo or prn.

notes.author: Otolaryngologist
notes.text:
Otolaryngology Consultation
Date: 09/19/2026
Patient: Lean Stanton, 65yo F

65yo W referred for HGNS eval. Pt c/o snoring and mild daytime somnolence. No hx of apnea tx. Exam: Tonsils 1+, no other obstruction. Nasal passages patent. Oral cavity unremarkable.

DISE 09/12/2026: AP velum collapse, no CCC. No tongue base or epiglottic collapse noted. No laryngeal obstruction.

Assessment: Findings consistent with velopharyngeal obstruction without concentric collapse. Candidate for HGNS therapy.

Plan: Discuss HGNS options, proceed with pre-op workup, and schedule follow-up.
